key_insight: EEG-Xplain unifies multiple attribution methods to make black-box EEG foundation models interpretable across spatial, temporal, and frequency dimensions.
engineering_relevance: It provides a standardized way to validate model reliability and physiological plausibility, supporting safer clinical and neuroscience use of EEG foundation models.
method: Combines gradient-, perturbation-, and activation-based explanations across heterogeneous EEG architectures.
Maps important channels, time segments, and frequency bands using topographic maps, attribution heatmaps, and spectral perturbation.
Assesses explanation quality with population-level AOPC and cross-method consistency, then converts results into LLM-generated natural-language reports.
evidence_signal: Experiments on Mumtaz2016 and TUAB show explanations aligned with known neurophysiological markers while also revealing artifact and spurious-pattern dependencies.
watch_item: Attributions can still reflect dataset artifacts or method-specific biases, so explanation results should be validated carefully across cohorts and models.
paper_title: EEG-Xplain: Decoding Neural Black-Boxes of EEG Foundation Models
